title: 37.6 A 22nm 60.81TFLOPS/W Diffusion Accelerator with Bandwidth-Aware Memory Partition and BL-Segmented Compute-in-Memory for Efficient Multi-Task Content Generation
problem: Existing CIM accelerators struggle with diffusion model efficiency due to: large operational intensity variation across layers creating dynamic bandwidth needs, 10x larger data storage than GANs/VAEs, system-level CIM efficiency degradation despite high macro efficiency, 59% CIM power consumed on data access, and 31% of operations spent on computationally-intensive multi-view/temporal attention.
motivation: Diffusion models enable high-quality multi-task content generation (images, 3D, video) but consuming ~270s on A100 GPU; hardware acceleration is critical for practical deployment.
method: The 22nm accelerator performs calculations directly in memory (compute-in-memory or CIM) instead of moving data back and forth, saving power. It splits memory into sections that match each layer's actual data needs (bandwidth-aware partitioning) and divides memory access paths using bit-line segmentation, keeping data local and reducing movement. These optimizations especially help tasks requiring multi-view or temporal attention—comparing multiple camera angles or frames over time—which are common in 3D and video generation.
key_novelty: It solves the problem of varying data needs across layers by using bandwidth-aware memory partitioning and bit-line segmentation in compute-in-memory, which cuts data-access power without sacrificing computational efficiency.
contributions: 60.81 TFLOPS/W energy efficiency for multi-task diffusion inference
Bandwidth-aware memory partition matching layer-wise operational intensity
BL-segmented CIM macros reducing system-level data-access overhead
Integrated multi-view/temporal attention operators for 3D/video consistency
primary_theme: Bandwidth-optimized CIM accelerator for multi-task diffusion inference
